title: Training Note: Loss Payee Notice Days When a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy Is Cancelled
content:
When a Cardinal Personal Auto Policy is cancelled at the named insured's request, lenders recorded as loss payees are owed notice. The loss payee notice days of a cancellation follow the policy's loss payee entries: every lienholder change entry on the policy's transaction history, across all of its vehicles, each marked as a new loan or a loan paid off.

## The rule

| Policy's loss payee entries | Loss payee notice days of the cancellation |
|---|---|
| More new loans than loan payoffs recorded on the policy | 10 days: the notice owed to a loss payee whose interest is still open |
| The policy's latest loan payoff took effect after the cancellation date | The calendar days from the cancellation date to the payoff's effective date, at most 10: the lender's interest stayed covered until it was paid off |
| Otherwise (latest payoff on or before the cancellation date, or no loan recorded) | None: the lender's interest ended before the cancellation |

The first matching line decides. A payoff counts by its effective date, whenever it was recorded.

## Questions answered (hypothetical; cancellation date 1 May 2026)

**Two vehicles each carry a new loan entry; one of them shows a loan paid off effective 1 March 2026.**
Two new loans against one payoff is more new loans than payoffs, so the notice days are 10.

**One new loan and one payoff effective 6 May 2026.**
Loans and payoffs are equal, and the payoff took effect after the cancellation date: 5 days (1 to 6 May).

**One new loan and one payoff effective 25 May 2026.**
That is 24 days after the cancellation date, held to at most 10: 10 days.

**One new loan and one payoff effective 1 May 2026, the cancellation date itself.**
The payoff is not after the cancellation date: none.

**No lienholder change entries on the policy.**
None.
